Wave Sounds for Natural Disasters and Personal Emergencies
Instant early warning to safeguard human life in confined spaces.

SOSistem™ is a system of sensors and terminals (displays) for real-time observation and information, installed indoors and outdoors, for human security. It keeps a real-time count of the people inside each space, like a physical inventory for evacuation and rescue; without cameras, it detects anyone who has fallen or stopped moving, alerts with light, sound and Morse code, and notifies the attendant, the monitoring center and 911 within seconds.

How is it different from a home sensor?

Consumer mmWave sensors with fall detection that alert a home app already exist. S.O.S.© is built for public venues and workplaces: it escalates the alert up to 911 with a CAP v1.2 message and SIP call, runs 30 days without mains power and shows occupancy and emergency signals in the NOM-026-STPS-2008 safety colors.

International catalog of safety signs with their pictogram, color and shape: safe condition and evacuation (E, green), fire protection (F, red), mandatory action (M, blue), prohibition (P, red) and warning (W, yellow).

Screens, lights and buttons use those colors according to the state; the facility's physical signage uses the registered pictograms, such as E001/E002 emergency exit, E003 first aid, E007 evacuation assembly point and W001 general warning. New edition in preparation (ISO/DIS 7010).
Design principles for safety signs and safety markings · confirmed in 2022

Defines the safety colors, their contrast colors and the geometric shapes: circle with diagonal bar for prohibition, circle for mandatory action, triangle for warning, and square or rectangle for safe condition and fire equipment.

Each state has a single color pair: red with white (emergency), yellow with black (warning), green with white (safe) and blue with white (information); reference colorimetry in ISO 3864-4 (RAL 3001, 1003, 6032 and 5005).
Design of graphical symbols for safety signs · 3rd ed., replaces the 2012 edition
Rules for drawing safety pictograms: symbol area, line thickness, standardized human figure and legibility at a distance.
S.O.S.©'s own symbols (person on the floor, earthquake and occupancy) are drawn under these rules; they are not signs registered in ISO 7010 and are identified as system symbols.

Tap a color to change it. Each fault must keep its safety color family (ISO 3864-1 and NOM-026-STPS-2008); if the shade leaves the family or loses contrast, it is flagged in amber. Changes are saved on this device.
